messages.author: da63f9ca4e626114
messages.subject: NA's Random Effects
parts:
Hi,
I would like to adjust the model:
Y = mu + block + genotype + genotype *environment + error
I managed to adjust it in lme4 via REML and would like to do the same with INLA.
Considering random genotype and genotype*environment.
My problem and that:
m1 $ summary.random
The coding of genotypes is NA.
Code:
require(INLA)
require(lme4)

dados <- expand.grid(gen=factor(paste('G',1:10,sep='')),local=factor(paste('l',1:5,sep='')),bloco=factor(paste('b',1:3,sep='')))
X <- cbind(1,model.matrix(~-1+gen,dados),model.matrix(~-1+local,dados))
dados$resp <- X %*% c(10,1:10,1:5) + rnorm(nrow(dados),0,2)
head(dados)

op <- options(contrasts=c("contr.sum", "contr.poly"))
m0 <- lmer(resp~bloco+(1|gen)+(1|local:gen),dados)
summary(m0)

formu <- resp ~ as.factor(bloco) + f(gen,model="iid") + f(as.factor(local:gen),model="iid")
m1 <- inla(formu,family="gaussian",data=dados,verbose=0)
summary(m1)

1/m1$summary.hyperpar[,1]
m1$summary.random

Thanks
Éder

messages.author: b453c29749de564d
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] NA's Random Effects
parts:
you're right.

inla has an issue when the 'arg', in 'f(arg,....)' is not numeric, then
these values are converted to numerical values and the actual
non-numeric values of 'arg' is lost. in your case there was a
'as.numeric()' that was missing. I have rebuildt the package, so if you
do inla.upgrade(testing=T), you're done.

the issue about the labels is on the TODO list, as if

i = factor(c("a","b"))

and

formula = y ~ f(i,....)

one would expect that you could find the marginal for level "a"
somewhere, but you cannot, as these are converted to numerics

> as.numeric(factor(c("a","b")))


so "a" is "1".

this wasn't done correct from the beginning in the implementation, and
its messy.

I'll see what I can do.

H
